# Documents of the worked example

**31 documents, 345 pages**, generated by [`tools/document.py`](../../../tools/document.py) from the item
files of this example. Nobody typed them: each document is assembled from the requirements,
architecture, design, tests, records, plans and analyses in this folder's sibling directories,
and states the commit it was built from (`68d1561`) and the hash of every item it shows. None is
marked DRAFT, because every item they show is approved.

| Format | Documents |
|---|---|
| PDF | 31 |
| HTML | 31 |
| Word | 3 |
| Excel | 3 |

**All content is invented demonstration data**, like the rest of the example.

## Formats

- **PDF** is the HTML printed on A4 with page numbers; GitHub shows it in the browser.
- **HTML** is the native output, one self-contained file; GitHub shows it as source, so download it
  and open it in a browser. Diagrams are drawn by Mermaid when the browser is online.
- **Word** uses a neutral style here; with a customer's `.docx` or `.dotx` template (`--template`,
  or `documents.template` in `project.yaml`) it takes the customer's styles.
- **Excel** has one sheet per chapter; a customer's workbook can be filled through a map file.

## Build them again

```
python tools/document.py --project examples/power-window list
python tools/document.py --project examples/power-window build software-architecture-description --format pdf
```

A build writes to `build/documents/`, which is not tracked. This folder is a snapshot taken at
commit `68d1561`; it is not updated when the items change.

Not shown, because the example has nothing to put in them yet: system integration test specification, system integration test report, system qualification test specification, system qualification test report, release note, risk management plan and register, supplier selection and monitoring report, self-assessment report, weaknesses and vulnerabilities.
